correctness.rationale: A positive-definite 2x2 Fourier Gram matrix gives the exact fixed-gap quotient. For d>=2, |sinc d|<=1/d bounds the quotient strictly by two. For 0<d<2, F_d(1)>0 follows from h double derivative, while F_d derivative positivity follows from an exact positive polynomial 3(1-u²)-d²u=d⁴(160-d⁴)/4800. Confluent affine representer proves sharpness and nonattainment; Taylor algebra proves the strictly positive quadratic deficit. Exact polynomial certificate and 13160 standard-library numerical checks corroborate calculations; analytical reasoning establishes all quantifiers and boundary cases.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 sparse Fourier exterior-regression framework leaves the exact leading pointwise amplification unknown. This result determines a natural continuous all-frequency minimax constant for the smallest nontrivial sparse model at every exterior distance, identifies unavoidable nonattainment through frequency collision, and quantifies a sharp quadratic gap penalty. This is information relevant to sharp regression leverage design and stability, not merely computation of a fixed 2x2 Gram inverse.
